name: syllabic_grain_stutter
title: Reverse syllables, narrow formants, stutter the phrase
material: articulated phrases with real gaps - speech, vocal phrases, sparse percussion
description: For material with genuine silences between events: grain reverse flips the order and content of the detected syllables, specfnu's narrow mode squeezes the formant bands, modify loudness rebalances, and envspeak repeats each detected syllable twice for a stutter.
source: Verified end-to-end on a formant-filtered 4-syllable vocal proxy in the Phase 5 generalization matrix (tests/test_generalization.py, vocal chain; docs/generalization-matrix.md).
notes: grain reverse REFUSES unarticulated material ('No grains found') and silently DISCARDS below-gate content on weakly-articulated beds (generalization finding) - it wants real silences.
envspeak at rand=0 is exactly indur * repet; raise rand for humanized timing.
sustained swells count as ONE syllable to envspeak (whole-file repeat) - articulation, not pitch, is what it detects.
